toc.title: How an LLM Works (the Parts the Exam Needs)
Model Options: Thinking, Effort and Fast Mode

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. LLM: large language model; SDK: software development kit; API: application programming interface; JSON: JavaScript Object Notation

  • LLM basics: tokens, context windows, sampling, non-determinism, next-token generation
  • Model options: fast mode, adaptive and extended thinking, effort levels
  • Fundamental prompting techniques: zero-shot, single-shot, multi-shot
  • Technical fundamentals: SDKs that wrap REST APIs, streaming and websockets

2How an LLM Works (the Parts the Exam Needs)

Running case

Tidewater Meets Strange Behavior

  • The assistant gave two slightly different answers to the same question
  • A long claim file made it cut off a list in the middle of a sentence
  • A developer asks: "Is it broken?"

Concept What to know
Token A piece of text (a word, part of a word or punctuation). Models read, produce and bill in tokens; a token is not a word (a rough rule is about three quarters of a word of English per token)
Context window The maximum tokens the model can consider in one request, input plus output; current models offer up to 1 million tokens
max_tokens A cap on the output only; if reached, the reply is cut off (stop_reason: max_tokens)
Next-token generation The model predicts a probability for every possible next token, one is chosen, appended, and the process repeats
Sampling How the next token is chosen from the probabilities (temperature, top-p, top-k control randomness)
Non-determinism The same prompt can give different wording each time; do not expect byte-identical output
Hallucination Fluent text that is not grounded in the input or facts; reduce with grounding, citations and validation
  • Why answers differ: sampling is random by design, and small changes in the prompt or context shift the probabilities. For repeatable behavior, constrain the output (structured output, clear instructions, evals) rather than hope for identical text.
  • Why output was cut off: a long reply reached max_tokens; raise the cap or ask for a shorter answer (not a bug).

[Verify live] On current models the sampling parameters temperature, top_p and top_k are not supported: a non-default value returns a 400 error. Guide behavior with prompting and effort instead. On older models they could be set (low temperature for more consistent, high for more varied output). As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Questions about "making output more random or more consistent" test the concept (sampling and non-determinism); on current models the practical levers are prompt design, structured output and effort.

3Model Options: Thinking, Effort and Fast Mode

Option What it changes Trade-off
Adaptive thinking The model decides how much to reason before answering Better on hard problems; thinking tokens cost output price and time
Extended thinking Old name A manual reasoning budget on older models Rejected on current models
Effort low to max: overall thoroughness and token use Higher = better quality and slower, costlier
Fast mode Faster output at a premium price on supported models Pay more for speed

(The request parameters are in Module 3; here you need to know what each is for.)

Exam tip

Effort and thinking trade quality for cost and latency; fast mode trades price for speed.

4Fundamental Prompting Techniques

Technique What it is Use it when
Zero-shot Instructions only, no examples The task is simple and well described
Single-shot (one-shot) One example of input and output You need to show the format or style
Multi-shot (few-shot) Several examples, including tricky cases Consistency matters or the task is ambiguous; examples teach the pattern better than long rules
  • Examples should be diverse and representative, include edge cases, and match the exact output format you want.

5Technical Fundamentals

  • SDKs wrap REST APIs. The official Python and TypeScript SDKs build the HTTP request, add headers, parse JSON, retry transient errors, and offer streaming helpers. You can call the REST endpoint directly, but the SDK saves effort and handles retries.
  • Authentication is an API key sent with the request (the SDK reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); cloud platforms use their own identity (Module 3).
  • Streaming uses server-sent events (SSE) over HTTP: one-way, server to client, simple through proxies. Websockets are a two-way, persistent connection used by some real-time products; know the difference: SSE is one-way text streaming, websockets are full-duplex.
  • Timeouts and retries: set client timeouts that fit long generations; use exponential backoff; make retries safe (Module 1).
  • Context management is an application job (Module 9): the API does not trim your history for you.

Exam tip

SSE streams one way over HTTP (the Messages API streaming); websockets keep a two-way connection.

6Exam Q&A

S1A developer sends the same prompt twice and gets two slightly different answers. What does this show?

  • AThe context window is full, so the model starts to drop earlier turns
  • BThe API key expired
  • COutput generation is sampled, so wording can vary between runs
  • DThe API is broken
Show the answer

Answer: C. Next-token sampling makes outputs non-deterministic; use constraints and evals for consistency.

S2A reply stops mid-sentence and stop_reason is max_tokens. What is the right interpretation?

  • AThe model refused
  • BThe output reached the max_tokens cap and was truncated
  • CThe context window of the model is too small for the prompt
  • DThe prompt contained an error
Show the answer

Answer: B. max_tokens limits output; reaching it truncates the answer.

S3What is a token?

  • AA piece of text, such as a word or part of a word, that models read, produce and bill in
  • BA characters-per-second measure of how quickly the model writes its reply
  • CAlways exactly one word
  • DA security credential
Show the answer

Answer: A. Tokens are the units of text for context limits and pricing.

S4What does the context window limit?

  • AThe number of API keys
  • BThe total tokens the model considers in one request, including its output
  • CThe size of the files on disk
  • DOnly the length of the model's reply and nothing about the size of the input
Show the answer

Answer: B. The window covers input plus output for the request.

S5A developer wants to show the model the exact output layout with one worked example. Which technique is this?

  • AStreaming
  • BZero-shot
  • CFine-tuning
  • DSingle-shot
Show the answer

Answer: D. One input and output example is single-shot prompting.

S6Which task most benefits from multi-shot prompting?

  • AAsking for the current time
  • BAn ambiguous classification with edge cases where consistency matters
  • CA trivial arithmetic question that any single instruction already answers
  • DA request for a poem
Show the answer

Answer: B. Several diverse examples teach the pattern and edge-case handling.

S7What is the practical difference between SSE and websockets?

  • AThey are identical
  • BSSE is one-way server-to-client streaming; websockets are two-way
  • CSSE is two-way and persistent; websockets are one-way and short-lived
  • DSSE needs no network
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Messages API streams over SSE; websockets are full-duplex.

S8Why use an official SDK instead of raw HTTP calls?

  • ASDKs make the model smarter and more accurate on hard tasks than raw HTTP
  • BIt wraps the REST API, handles headers, parsing, streaming helpers and retries of transient errors
  • CRaw HTTP is not possible
  • DSDKs remove rate limits
Show the answer

Answer: B. SDKs reduce boilerplate and add retry and streaming support.

S9A developer tries to set temperature on a current model and gets a 400 error. What should they do?

  • ARemove the parameter and guide behavior with prompts, structure and effort
  • BSwitch to an older model family that still accepts it and keep the same code
  • CContact billing
  • DRetry with a higher temperature
Show the answer

Answer: A. Current models do not accept non-default sampling parameters.

S10Which TWO statements about generation are correct? Select TWO.

  • AIdentical prompts always return identical text
  • BA larger context window removes the need to manage context
  • CThe model predicts the next token one at a time from the context
  • DHallucinations can be reduced with grounding and validation
  • ETokens are always whole words
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. Generation is next-token prediction, and grounding and validation reduce hallucination; outputs vary and tokens are not words.

S11Which TWO describe fast mode and effort correctly? Select TWO.

  • AEffort changes the model's context window size
  • BLower effort usually reduces cost and latency with some capability loss
  • CFast mode is free
  • DFast mode delivers faster output at premium pricing
  • EEffort is a strict token budget
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Fast mode buys speed at a premium and effort is a behavioral signal that trades quality for cost and latency.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Token Piece of text; basis of limits and billing
Context window Max tokens in one request (input + output); up to 1M on current models
max_tokens Output cap; hitting it truncates
Generation Next-token prediction, one token at a time, sampled
Non-determinism Same prompt can vary; constrain with structure and evals
Sampling params temperature, top_p, top_k: concept; not supported on current models (400 error)
Model options Adaptive thinking · effort (low … max) · fast mode (speed at a premium)
Shots Zero-shot (instructions) · single-shot (one example) · multi-shot (several, with edge cases)
Transport SDKs wrap REST; SSE = one-way stream; websockets = two-way connection
